notes: מַה־לְּךָ → *What aileth thee*: מָה takes *What*, the predicate לְ takes *aileth* as the relational verb written where the copula would stand (rules 49, 20), the suffix takes *thee*; the noncompositional *What aileth* reading was set aside because *What* is separably מָה's.

Both *that*s go to the one כִּי: the second colon is the gapped parallel of the first with no conjunction of its own, so the rewritten subordinator is the morpheme's distributed realization (rules 25, 34) rather than an `added` word; the `added` reading under rule 55 is the competing one. Contrast v6, where the כִּי is not in the verse (rule 10).
Vocative articles are `unrepresented`; the nouns take *O thou* and *Thou* (rule 36); each imperfect keeps its own *thou* (rule 17).
